intentions.welcome: Great. You can learn the basics here with no commitment. Deciding fish farming isn't for you is a perfectly good outcome too.

intentions.label: I'm thinking about starting
intentions.welcome: Good. Water is the first thing to check, so that's where we'll begin.

intentions.label: I'm studying agriculture
intentions.welcome: Welcome. This lesson connects what you study with the practical questions a beginner faces on a real site.

understandingCheck.question: Why isn't rain alone a reliable way to fill a fish pond?
options: Dry periods can leave the pond too low
Catfish cannot live in rain water

understandingCheck.question: African catfish can breathe air. What does that mean for water?
options: They are hardy, but good water is still needed

understandingCheck.question: Water from a source looks clear. What is a sensible next step before relying on it?
options: Nothing, clear water is always fine

stuckHints.lesson: Try reading just wa-03 (Enough water, all year round). It holds the single most important idea in this lesson.
stuckHints.activity-observe: Start small: write what the source is, who uses it, and one thing you don't know about it in the dry season.
stuckHints.activity-questions: Copy two questions from the lesson checklist (wa-09) and add one of your own about the specific place.
stuckHints.activity-fictional: Re-read Amina's story and look for three facts: what happened in the dry season, where the stream is compared with the plot, and whether anything was tested.
stuckHints.guide: Try asking about one idea at a time, for example: 'Why does the dry season matter?'

nextSteps.label: Find out if there is a fisheries extension agent or fish culture station near you
Talk to an experienced local catfish farmer about their water
Ask people who use your water source how it behaves in the driest months
Find out where water can be tested in your area
Pause here. You've learned the first thing to check, and you can come back any time

unsupportedFallback.message: The lessons here don't cover that yet, so I can't give you a reliable answer.
